importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation between sub-types (single vs double ATM, kiosk vs walk-in, MS vs ACP-clad exterior). Buyers scan listing images to confirm this is an ATM-specific cabin — not a generic security or office cabin — before reading any text. Wrong product type is an immediate skip.

Wall material, cabin configuration (single/double ATM), key provisions (AC, wiring, CCTV), and security grade are primary shortlisting gates. A cabin missing required provisions cannot be used regardless of price — specs must match deployment requirements before any further evaluation.

Price varies substantially with wall material (MS vs PUF panel), cabin configuration (single vs double ATM), and fit-out provisions. Indian institutional buyers compare prices aggressively but only after confirming spec equivalence — listed price is a budget entry point, with final price negotiated for batch orders.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in prefab ATM cabins — market is fragmented across regional fabricators; buyers search by spec and deployment track record, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional buyers (banks, WLA operators) evaluate manufacturer status, prior bank/WLA deployment track record, installation capability, and after-sales service for multi-site rollouts. Company credentials are a vendor qualification signal, not a primary shortlisting filter.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per sq ft quoting exists for custom-dimensioned builds but per piece dominates all standard catalogue transactions. No buyer questions whether a complete ATM cabin is sold per piece.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied — a complete factory-built ATM cabin is always sold per piece. No buyer confusion risk exists.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the fundamental cabin configuration (Kiosk / Single ATM / Double ATM / Cash Recycler) — non-interchangeable sub-types with entirely different footprints, layouts, and the largest price delta in the category.

Determines construction quality tier and thermal/structural performance (MS vs PUF vs FRP vs ACP) — non-interchangeable for climate-specific deployments and drives significant price variation between values.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Wall panel thickness (e.g., 50mm / 75mm / 100mm for PUF panels) is a primary structural and thermal insulation differentiator that directly affects price and suitability for hot-climate or high-security deployments — buyers in semi-urban and rural India specifically compare this.

Roof type (flat MS sheet vs insulated sandwich panel vs sloped GI sheet) affects thermal performance and weather resistance — a key differentiator for outdoor ATM deployments in varied Indian climates that buyers compare when specifying cabins for rural or coastal sites.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Construction material defines the cabin's structural and thermal performance tier — sellers need this to confirm manufacturing capability and price accurately across MS, PUF, FRP, and ACP variants.
Fit-out provisions (AC, wiring, UPS, CCTV, glow sign) directly determine manufacturing scope and price — sellers need to know which provisions are required to respond with an accurate quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires a single ATM, double ATM, kiosk, or cash recycler cabin — this determines the entire footprint, layout, and structural specification, and routes the RFQ to sellers who manufacture that specific configuration.
